When is skiing worth the trip?

December 1–April 30, in seven-day periods. One graph compares the typical modeled condition index across all 19 mountains with Magic, Bolton and Jay. It uses historical inputs and your current scoring weights; it does not depend on which trips the solver selects.

The shaded band is the middle 50% of mountain scores, not a confidence interval. The dashed line is your minimum. Monthly depth and terrain evidence are combined with ten winters of weekly weather averages. Monthly evidence cannot resolve week-to-week snowpack changes, and sparse reports can favor operating days. Unknown components use the documented fallback.

A condition index is not a probability. A score of 80 does not mean an 80% chance of great skiing. We lack consistent dated observations of snow depth, terrain availability and skiing quality across historical seasons, so an empirical “chance of great skiing” cannot be estimated from this snapshot. The graph also does not establish whether a mountain was operating. Let the evidence show which periods score better; late March is not guaranteed to beat December every year.

Mixed-integer formulation

Let W be the weekends, Tw the feasible complete itineraries for weekend w, and M the mountains. Each itinerary contains both ski days and its lodging base, or staying home.

Decision variable
xwt ∈ {0, 1}: choose itinerary t for weekend w.

First objective
Q* = max Σw∈W Σt∈Tw qwt xwt

Second objective
min Σw∈W Σt∈Tw cwt xwt, subject to Σ qwtxwt ≥ Q* − 0.01.

Weekend constraint
Σt∈Tw xwt = Aw for every w.

Pass capacity
Σw,t awtmxwt ≤ Lm for every m.

Aw is your active toggle (0 or 1); inactive weekends are omitted from the generated solver model. awtm counts visits to mountain m in itinerary t (0, 1 or 2). Lm is the remaining pass allowance, capped at two for every Indy mountain even if a stored input is larger. cwt is the party's full trip cost. qwt is the quality score scaled by 1,000 and rounded to an integer. The 0.01 tolerance is in those scaled units, so integer quality is preserved exactly when the first solve is optimal.

qwt / 1000 ≈ Σd∈{Sat,Sun} hd(0.55 smd + 0.30 pm + 0.15 gmd − ρ bmd) − λ Dwt

h: ski hours; s: the chosen historical condition index; p: mountain preference; g: crowd factor including holiday adjustment; b: poor-weather frequency; ρ: risk penalty; λ: drive fatigue penalty; D: total itinerary driving hours. The first three weights are fixed model assumptions: 55%, 30%, 15%. Preferences, crowd factors, ρ and λ are editable.

Two-day season limit for every mountain

Σw,t awtmxwt ≤ 2 for every mountain m, including Epic.

This is a separate planning constraint from pass access. A Saturday and Sunday at one mountain consume both days. The bound is hard-coded in the solver and checked after solving, so saved inputs cannot bypass it. Some weekends may remain unscheduled once eligible mountains reach the limit.

Required Magic weekend

Σ(w,t): Sat = Magic, Sun = Magic, hSat = hSun = 7 xwt = 1

The solver must select exactly one full two-day Magic trip. If you pin its date, only that weekend can satisfy the constraint. Combined with the two-day Indy cap, this prevents every additional Magic visit. Inactive or infeasible dates produce a clear error rather than violating the requirement.

Time constraints encoded in the feasible itinerary set

  • Adjusted road time τij = nominal routing time × (1 + traffic allowance / 100).
  • Day trip: τhome,m ≤ 2 hours by default.
  • Hotel trip: Friday departure + τhome,hotel ≤ Friday arrival deadline; two nights at the same base; each hotel/mountain commute ≤ the configured limit.
  • Sunday ski hours h = min(7, home deadline − τmountain,home − 0.5 − 9). Trips with less than two Sunday ski hours are excluded.
  • Mountain must fall within its assumed opening/closing dates on each ski day.
  • Each ski day must have condition index × 100 ≥ the minimum (default 70). No preference or cost can override this hard eligibility rule.

There is no budget constraint. Every mountain has a hard season limit of two ski days, regardless of pass type. The model does not use hotel cost to choose a slightly worse-scoring itinerary.

A real binary itinerary model

Each binary variable selects one complete weekend itinerary: Saturday mountain, Sunday mountain, and either home or a two-night lodging base. Staying home is also feasible. Mountains may differ each day.

1. Maximize quality-adjusted ski hours minus weather risk and drive fatigue.
2. Hold the best score fixed; minimize total trip cost.

Each active weekend selects exactly one itinerary. Indy visits consume two included days per mountain over the season. Epic access is unrestricted, but the separate season visit cap still limits each mountain to two planned days. All travelers are assumed to have the same access. Paid extra Indy days are excluded.

Friday travel begins after work and must meet the hotel-arrival deadline. Day trips are eligible only within the drive-time threshold, including traffic allowance. Sunday skiing ends early if required to get home by 8 p.m. Both nights use the same lodging town, with a maximum commute to each mountain. Roads and travel times are directional. Mount Snow uses the base-area location from Vermont environmental records; its original summit-area routing point was corrected.

Condition index: evidence and explicit assumptions

The new mode combines monthly reported base depth, observed terrain-open percentage, and a recent-snow/rain surface proxy. Temperature alone is not a penalty, so warm spring skiing is not automatically classified as poor. The original cold-weather score is retained as a comparison mode.

Depth component D = min(reported monthly average depth / depth saturation, 1)
Terrain component T = reported monthly open-terrain fraction, used only when report count meets your minimum.
Surface proxy S = mean over historical days of clamp(0.65 + 0.25 × min(7-day snow cm / 25, 1) − 0.30 × min(3-day rain mm / 15, 1), 0.05, 1).

Condition index = weighted mean of available D, T, S.
Defaults: 40% depth, 40% terrain, 20% recent weather; depth saturation 24 inches; minimum 3 terrain reports.

Missing depth and terrain data remain unknown; weights are renormalized over the available components. Terrain below the minimum report count is shown but excluded. If no weighted observed component is available, the recent-weather proxy is used and labeled as a fallback. The risk term uses the fraction of S < 0.45 multiplied by the effective weather weight. It is a weather-disruption proxy, not an estimated probability of poor skiing.

These weights, saturation depth, and report threshold are planning assumptions. They have not been calibrated against skier enjoyment or validated as a forecast. Reported depths are not directly comparable terrain-coverage measurements, and volunteer reports are not a random sample. Monthly means conceal date-level melt, wind closures, glade availability, grooming and freeze/thaw cycles. Sparse April observations may describe only days when a resort was operating.

The retained original mode uses the earlier temperature/snow/rain heuristic: clamp(0.58 + 0.25 × min(7-day snow cm / 25, 1) + 0.12 × [max temp < 1°C] − 0.22 × min(3-day rain mm / 15, 1) − 0.18 × min(max(max temp − 3, 0) / 10, 1), 0.05, 1). Comparing modes keeps the two-day cap, Magic requirement, travel rules and preferences unchanged.

Either mode feeds the same objective: 55% condition index, 30% mountain preference and 15% crowd factor, multiplied by ski hours, minus weather disruption and drive fatigue. Source data changes the coefficient inputs; the binary MIP constraints stay the same.

  • Epic Northeast resort directory. Full unrestricted Epic access is assumed from your no-blackout instruction.
  • Hotel rates, preferences, parking and season dates: editable planning assumptions. Prices are estimates until overridden with dated quotes.
  • GLPK.js · genuine mixed-integer solver running in your browser. GPL license.

No money ceiling is imposed. Costs include fuel, lodging, parking, food and entered extras. Pass purchase, rentals, equipment, tolls and vehicle wear are excluded unless added to extras. An active weekend is available, not mandatory; the model can select staying home.

Changes are saved in this browser. They do not sync across devices. Solve again after editing inputs. This is a seasonal planning snapshot; weather forecasts and hotel quotes do not refresh automatically.
